saints.name: St. Julie Billiart
saints.title: Virgin and Founder
saints.shortBlurb: A French peasant woman, long paralyzed, who rose to found the Sisters of Notre Dame de Namur…
biography: Born at Cuvilly in Picardy in 1751, a farmer's daughter, Julie Billiart knew the catechism by heart at seven and soon taught it to others. In 1774 she witnessed a shot fired at her father; the shock brought on an illness that slowly paralyzed her, and by 1784 she was bedridden — yet from her bed she taught catechism and prepared children for first communion.

During the Revolution she sheltered hunted priests and had to be smuggled out of Cuvilly under straw in a wagon, reaching Amiens, where in 1794 she met the noblewoman Françoise Blin de Bourdon. With her and Catherine Duchâtel she founded the Sisters of Notre Dame at Amiens on 2 February 1804 to teach poor girls; that same year, after a novena prescribed by her confessor, she was completely cured.

The motherhouse moved to Namur in 1809, and as the Sisters of Notre Dame de Namur the institute spread: in twelve years Julie founded fifteen convents and made a hundred and twenty journeys, her watchword 'How good is the good God'. She died at Namur on 8 April 1816, was beatified by Pius X in 1906, and canonized by Paul VI in 1969.
saints.knownFor: Founding the Sisters of Notre Dame de Namur for the education of poor girls.
